title: Day 4: Normalization
summary: Store each fact once: normal forms one through three, an orders and customers example, and the join-cost trade-off.

title: Day 5: Read replicas
summary: Read replicas: scale SELECTs off the primary, and live with replication lag.

title: Day 6: Leader–Follower replication
summary: Leader–follower replication: one writer, followers copy the log, lag and failover trade-offs.

title: Day 7: Multi-leader replication
summary: Multi-leader replication: several nodes accept writes for low-latency multi-region and offline use, at the cost of resolving write conflicts.

title: Day 8: Quorum
summary: Quorums: how R plus W greater than N lets replicated databases tolerate failures and still read recent writes.

title: Day 9: Consensus
summary: How Raft and Paxos get a cluster to agree on one answer, why etcd stops writes without a majority, and what that costs.

title: Day 10: CAP theorem
summary: CAP theorem: when the network splits, you choose consistency or availability, and PACELC adds latency to the everyday picture.

title: Day 11: BASE
summary: BASE: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent, the availability-first alternative to ACID and what it costs your app.

title: Day 12: ACID
summary: ACID: the four transaction guarantees, the write-ahead log, and why isolation levels still matter

title: Day 13: Eventual consistency
summary: Eventual consistency: replicas converge over time, trading fresh reads for speed and availability.

title: Day 14: Strong consistency
summary: Strong consistency: every read sees the latest write, and what that costs in latency and availability

title: Day 15: Snapshot isolation
summary: Snapshot isolation: consistent reads from a frozen view of the database, and the write skew trap

title: Day 16: MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control)
summary: MVCC: how databases keep multiple row versions so readers never block writers, and the cleanup cost that comes with it.

title: Day 17: Two-phase commit (2PC)
summary: Two-phase commit: how a coordinator gets several databases to vote, then commit or abort together, and why it blocks when the coordinator crashes.

title: Day 18: Three-phase commit (3PC)
summary: Three-phase commit adds a pre-commit step to avoid 2PC blocking, but breaks under network partitions.

title: Day 19: Write-ahead logging (WAL)
summary: Write-ahead logging: why databases write changes to an append-only log before touching data, and how that log powers crash recovery, replication and point-in-time restore.

title: Day 20: Checkpointing
summary: Checkpointing: how databases flush dirty pages and mark a safe point in the log so crash recovery stays fast and old log segments can be recycled.

title: Day 21: Compaction
summary: How LSM-tree databases merge old files, drop tombstones, and trade write, read, and space costs.

title: Day 22: Rebalancing
summary: How clusters move data between nodes as they grow, shrink, or get lopsided, and why eager rebalancing can turn a blip into an outage.

title: Day 23: Resharding
summary: Resharding: changing shard count or shard key while the system keeps running, how online reshards work, and why cutover is the scary part.

title: Day 24: Data locality
summary: Data locality: keep related data close to the code that uses it, and the latency trade-offs when you don't.

title: Day 25: Hot partition
summary: Hot partitions: when one shard takes all the heat and how systems cope
